title: Grassroots Democracy: Governance — Class 6 CBSE Social Science
subject: Social Science

slides.title: Grassroots Democracy — Governance
bullets: Class 6 — CBSE Social Science
Chapter 10 (Part 1)
slides.speaker_notes: How communities decide together — and how India does it.

slides.title: What you'll be able to do
bullets: Define governance and good governance.
Explain what democracy is.
Use the words SOVEREIGN / SECULAR / REPUBLIC.
Tell apart Union, State and Local government.
Explain the 73rd and 74th Amendments.
List ways to participate in democracy.

slides.title: What is governance?
bullets: Governance = how a community decides and gets things done.
Greek root = 'to steer'.
Three pillars: clear RULES, fair PROCESSES, ACCOUNTABILITY.
Happens at many scales: family, school, village, country.
Three big questions: WHO rules? HOW are decisions made? HOW is power limited?

slides.title: What is democracy?
bullets: Greek demos (people) + kratos (rule) → 'rule of the people'.
In a representative democracy, people elect representatives.
One person, one vote of EQUAL value.
Multiple parties and candidates can compete.
Power is LIMITED by a Constitution; citizens have RIGHTS.

slides.title: Different ways societies have answered
bullets: Ancient kingdoms — one king, his word is law.
Vajji confederacy (Buddha's time) — council of elders, decisions by discussion.
Modern monarchies — limited king + parliament.
Modern dictatorships — power without elections.
Modern democracies — people elect rulers, ruler is bound by law.

slides.title: India — the world's largest democracy
bullets: Independent on 15 August 1947.
Constitution came into effect on 26 January 1950 = Republic Day.
Drafting Committee chaired by Dr B. R. Ambedkar.
India is: SOVEREIGN, SOCIALIST, SECULAR, DEMOCRATIC, REPUBLIC.
Largest by number of voters — hundreds of millions in many languages.

slides.title: Five Preamble words — what they mean
bullets: SOVEREIGN — independent; no foreign country decides for us.
SOCIALIST — aims to reduce inequality.
SECULAR — no official religion; all religions equal.
DEMOCRATIC — people choose their government.
REPUBLIC — elected head of state, not a hereditary king.

slides.title: Three levels of government
bullets: UNION — defence, foreign affairs, currency, railways.
STATE — police, agriculture, much of education.
LOCAL — wells, street lights, schools, sanitation.
Three storeys of one building.
Each level handles different subjects.

slides.title: Sort the subject — which level?
bullets: Foreign affairs → Union.
State police → State.
Village street lights → Local.
Currency / Indian Rupee → Union.
Local sanitation → Local.

slides.title: Local government and Gram Swaraj
bullets: Local government is closest to ordinary people.
Rural = PANCHAYATI RAJ; Urban = Municipality / Nagar Panchayat.
Mahatma Gandhi: GRAM SWARAJ = village self-rule.
Strong villages → strong India.
Local bodies know local problems best.

slides.title: 73rd & 74th Amendments (1992)
bullets: Gave Panchayats and Municipalities a CONSTITUTIONAL foundation.
Required REGULAR ELECTIONS at the local level.
Reserved SEATS for women, Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes.
Gave a CLEAR LIST of powers and resources.
Turned local government from idea to reality across India.

slides.title: Rights and Duties
bullets: FUNDAMENTAL RIGHTS: equality, free speech, religion, fair laws.
FUNDAMENTAL DUTIES: respect Constitution and flag, protect public property, safeguard environment.
Vote at age 18.
Stand for elections; contact representatives.
Use RTI (Right to Information) to ask government for facts.

slides.title: Governance beyond elections
bullets: Free press — can criticise government without fear.
Independent judiciary — strikes down bad laws.
Strong institutions — Election Commission, CAG.
Active civil society — NGOs, citizens' groups, gram sabhas.
Together, they keep governance honest BETWEEN elections.

slides.title: You try (5 minutes)
bullets: 1. Define governance in one sentence.
2. List 3 features of a democracy.
3. Match: defence / police / well → Union / State / Local.
4. Why are the 73rd and 74th Amendments important?
5. Name 2 Fundamental Rights and 2 Fundamental Duties.

slides.title: Quick check
bullets: Q1. Who chairs the Drafting Committee of the Constitution?
Q2. Voting age in India?
Q3. SECULAR means?
Q4. Which level handles foreign affairs?
Show fingers.

slides.title: Key takeaways
bullets: Governance = decide + act fairly. Democracy = rule by the people.
India: independent 15 Aug 1947, Republic 26 Jan 1950 — Sovereign, Socialist, Secular, Democratic, Republic.
Three levels: Union, State, Local.
Local government — Panchayati Raj + Municipalities — closest to the people.
73rd & 74th Amendments (1992) gave local government constitutional backing.
Citizens have RIGHTS and DUTIES; participation is the heart of democracy.
Free press, courts, institutions, civil society keep governance honest.
